submitted.rationale: Index 15 (In0.49Sb0.51, at the InSbO4 composition) had the highest measured EQE: 0.0871%. MACE puts InSbO4 on the hull, and MEGNet predicts an HSE gap of 2.2 eV, below the 2.4 eV photon energy. The other measured points came in lower but close: index 6 (In11Sb3O24 composition) at 0.0793% and index 11 (two-phase mixture) at 0.0792%.

rejected.reason: In11Sb3O24 is stable and has the smallest predicted gap (1.9 eV), but its measured EQE of 0.0793% is below index 15.
In the two-phase region, EQE 0.0792%; mixing the two phases gave no benefit.
Not measured because the budget ran out. In3Sb5O12 is 0.018 eV/atom above the hull and has a predicted gap of 2.77 eV, above the 2.4 eV photon energy, so it is a less likely absorber.

consultations.verdict: Support: In11Sb3O24 (In 0.786) is on the MACE hull (0 eV/atom) with the smallest predicted HSE gap (1.91 eV < 2.4 eV photon energy) of the ternaries; index 6 (In 0.7885) matches this stoichiometry.

Support: InSbO4 (In 0.5) is on the MACE hull, and MEGNet puts its HSE gap at 2.2 eV, below the 2.4 eV photons. That makes index 15 (In 0.493) the second-best-motivated single-phase region after In11Sb3O24. In3Sb5O12 is slightly off the hull and its gap is 2.77 eV, so it is less favoured.

Uninformative to mildly supportive. Sb2O3 has a predicted gap of 2.2 eV, so the Sb-rich end is not clearly better. Index 11 (In 0.626) falls in the two-phase In11Sb3O24 + InSbO4 region, between two measured points with similar EQE (~0.08%). Both end phases have gaps below 2.4 eV and are on the hull, so a heterojunction mixture could plausibly do better. The GP UCB also ranks index 11 highest.
